top_choice_rationale: P001 (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) rewards one idea, small-molecule induced proximity between an E3 ligase and a chosen protein, in two chemistries: the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues (Handa). The chemistry is explicit (ligand and linker design, ternary-complex cooperativity), widely reproduced, and the credit divides along a defensible concept/mechanism line. The unapproved status of degraders and the exclusion of Ciulli and Ito are real costs, but I treat them as timing and cut-off issues, not as lack of merit. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles follow as the most mature alternative, with the early Vancouver formulation and phase-behaviour work (P004) preferred over the Cullis/Anderson plus base editing pairing (P003), which adds a young second part. Hartwig and Buchwald come next as mature and cleanly credited but close to the 2010 prize, then zeolite design; no award is last.
